newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's January CPI up 1.65 pct vs 2.51 yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's January CPI up 1.65 pct vs 2.51 yr ago.

text.p: Colombia's consumer price index rose 1.65 percent in January, well below the 2.51 percent increase during the same month last year, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said.
It said the increase, which brought inflation over the last 12 months to 20.62 percent, was the lowest for the month of January in 13 years.

The rise was slightly higher, however, than Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo had said it would be in remarks to reporters Thursday. Ocampo had said he expected the CPI number to print a full percentage point below January 1996.
A monthly increase in line with January's 1.65 percent would push inflation 1.8 percent above the ambitious 18 percent target the government and central bank have set for 1997.

Inflation in 1996 totaled a higher-than-expected 21.63 percent, well over the 17 percent target set for the entire year. The government has vowed nonetheless to hold most public sector workers to an average wage hike of 13.5 percent this year.

Unions representing about 800,000 public sector workers have set a February 11 deadline for an indefinite, nationwide strike in response to the wage offer and the government's calls for belt-tightening to narrow its burgeoning fiscal deficit.

Mauricio Cardenas, head of the respected economic think tank Fedesarrollo, revised his forecast for 1997 inflation earlier this week from 19 to 20 percent, citing what he called additional price pressures from the government's recent decision to clamp a six percent tax on all new foreign loans.
